title: Lung Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: DRAFT decision support authored from standard guidelines (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison) - physician decides. Full lung pathway by histology: NSCLC (workup -> clinical stage -> stage/driver/PD-L1/line-directed treatment -> surveillance -> recurrent/metastatic), small cell lung cancer (limited vs extensive vs relapsed), and malignant pleural mesothelioma (resectable vs advanced by histology). Each treatment leaf routes to APPLICABLE existing StewardMD Standard Protocols by reference; targeted agents and surgery/radiation without a dose protocol are shown as checklist guidance with NO dose. Workup/staging/biomarker content is original wording, not proprietary guideline text. Invents no dose/regimen/eligibility criterion. DRAFT - not clinically activated; the physician decides and the existing dose engine computes patient doses.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with standard guidelines (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison), NSCLC / SCLC / Mesothelioma. Regimen options reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols; the dose engine computes patient doses.

a.text: Test EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF V600E, KRAS G12C, MET exon-14, RET, NTRK and PD-L1 on every advanced non-squamous NSCLC (and never-smoker / young squamous). An actionable driver takes priority over first-line immunotherapy; do not start a checkpoint inhibitor while molecular results are pending if a targetable driver is plausible.

b.text: After definitive concurrent chemoradiation for unresectable stage III without progression, durvalumab consolidation improves progression-free and overall survival; PD-L1 >= 1% derives the greatest benefit in most regulatory labels.

c.text: For resected EGFR-mutant stage IB-IIIA NSCLC, adjuvant osimertinib prolongs disease-free survival; give after any indicated adjuvant chemotherapy.

d.text: In SCLC consider prophylactic cranial irradiation or MRI surveillance after response; add consolidative thoracic radiation in selected extensive-stage responders. Brain imaging is part of staging for all SCLC.

nodes.name: Histology
nodes.title: Confirmed histology
nodes.description: Lung cancer branches first by histology. Small cell and mesothelioma follow distinct pathways; within NSCLC, squamous vs non-squamous changes the chemotherapy backbone (pemetrexed is non-squamous only).
bullets: NSCLC - non-squamous (adenocarcinoma / large cell): full molecular panel
NSCLC - squamous cell carcinoma
Small cell lung cancer (SCLC)
Malignant pleural mesothelioma

nodes.name: NSCLC workup
nodes.title: NSCLC: workup and staging studies
nodes.description: Establish tissue diagnosis, molecular profile and accurate stage before committing to a curative or palliative track.
bullets: History, physical, smoking and performance status; weight and comorbidity review
Contrast CT chest/upper abdomen; PET-CT for candidates for curative therapy
Brain MRI for stage II or higher, or any neurologic symptom
Pathologic mediastinal staging (EBUS +/- mediastinoscopy) when it changes management

bullets.label: Molecular panel on non-squamous (and selected squamous)
bullets.sub: EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, KRAS G12C, MET exon-14, RET, NTRK plus PD-L1 TPS

bullets: Pulmonary function tests before resection or definitive radiation

nodes.name: NSCLC clinical stage
nodes.title: NSCLC: clinical stage / resectability
nodes.description: Select the clinical scenario. Early-stage and resectable locally advanced disease are curative-intent; unresectable stage III is chemoradiation with consolidation; stage IV is molecularly driven palliative therapy.

tables.title: NSCLC stage groups (simplified) and default track
rows: T1-2 N1 or T3 N0 M0
T3-4 N1 or selected N2, M0

nodes.name: Stage I NSCLC
nodes.title: Stage I NSCLC: surgery or SBRT
nodes.description: Curative local therapy; systemic therapy is generally not required at true stage I.
bullets: Lobectomy with mediastinal nodal sampling/dissection is the standard; sublobar resection for small peripheral tumors or limited reserve
Stereotactic body radiation (SBRT) for medically inoperable or patient-declined surgery
Adjuvant chemotherapy generally not indicated for stage IA; consider for high-risk resected IB
Adjuvant osimertinib if a resected tumor is EGFR-mutant (see footnote)

nodes.name: Resectable II-III NSCLC
nodes.title: Resectable stage II-IIIA NSCLC: perioperative therapy
nodes.description: Surgery combined with perioperative platinum-doublet chemotherapy plus immunotherapy; adjuvant targeted therapy for a driver mutation. Backbone matches histology.
bullets: Neoadjuvant platinum-doublet + a checkpoint inhibitor, then surgery (or adjuvant chemo +/- immunotherapy after upfront resection)
Pemetrexed doublet only for non-squamous; use a gemcitabine or paclitaxel doublet for squamous
Adjuvant osimertinib for resected EGFR-mutant disease; adjuvant alectinib for resected ALK-positive disease
Withhold perioperative immunotherapy when a targetable EGFR/ALK driver is present
Chemotherapy regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Unresectable III NSCLC
nodes.title: Unresectable stage III NSCLC: chemoradiation + durvalumab
nodes.description: Definitive concurrent platinum-doublet chemoradiation, then durvalumab consolidation in non-progressors. Backbone matches histology.
bullets: Concurrent platinum-doublet chemotherapy with thoracic radiation (60 Gy in conventional fractionation)
Pemetrexed doublet only for non-squamous; gemcitabine or paclitaxel doublet for squamous
Durvalumab consolidation for up to 1 year in patients without progression after chemoradiation
Reassess for targeted therapy if an EGFR/ALK driver is found (consolidation immunotherapy less favored)
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Actionable driver
nodes.title: Metastatic NSCLC: actionable molecular driver
nodes.description: In stage IV (or recurrent) NSCLC, an actionable driver directs first-line targeted therapy and takes priority over immunotherapy. Choose the dominant driver; if none, proceed to PD-L1.

tables.title: Actionable drivers in metastatic NSCLC and preferred first-line targeted agent

nodes.name: EGFR line of therapy
nodes.title: EGFR-mutant metastatic NSCLC: line of therapy
nodes.description: First-line uses a third-generation EGFR TKI. On progression, re-biopsy (tissue or plasma) to define resistance and switch to chemotherapy-based therapy.

nodes.name: EGFR first line
nodes.title: EGFR-mutant metastatic NSCLC: first-line TKI
nodes.description: A third-generation EGFR TKI is preferred over chemotherapy or immunotherapy first line.
bullets: Osimertinib is the preferred first-line agent (CNS activity, favorable tolerability)
Consider adding chemotherapy or amivantamab-based combinations for higher-risk disease per current labels
Do not use single-agent immunotherapy in EGFR-mutant disease (low benefit, added toxicity with sequential TKI)
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: EGFR post-TKI
nodes.title: EGFR-mutant NSCLC: after TKI progression
nodes.description: Re-biopsy to define resistance; most patients transition to platinum-doublet chemotherapy.
bullets: Re-test (tissue or plasma) for resistance mechanisms and histologic transformation (small-cell/squamous)
Platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy is the usual next step (non-squamous); consider adding a VEGF pathway or antibody-drug conjugate per current data
Osimertinib remains appropriate if progression occurred on an earlier-generation TKI with acquired T790M
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: ALK-positive
nodes.title: ALK-rearranged metastatic NSCLC: targeted therapy
nodes.description: A next-generation ALK TKI is preferred first line over chemotherapy or immunotherapy.
bullets: Preferred first-line: alectinib, brigatinib, or lorlatinib (strong CNS penetration)
On progression, switch to an alternative next-generation ALK TKI guided by resistance mutation, then platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy
Avoid single-agent immunotherapy in ALK-positive disease
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: ROS1-positive
nodes.title: ROS1-rearranged metastatic NSCLC: targeted therapy
nodes.description: A ROS1 TKI is preferred first line. No dedicated dose protocol here yet; regimen shown as guidance.
bullets: Preferred first-line: entrectinib or repotrectinib (CNS-active); crizotinib is an alternative without CNS disease
On progression: switch ROS1 TKI by resistance profile, then platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy (non-squamous)
No StewardMD dose protocol for ROS1 TKIs at present - prescribe per current label / dose engine

nodes.name: BRAF V600E
nodes.title: BRAF V600E metastatic NSCLC: targeted therapy
nodes.description: Combined BRAF + MEK inhibition. No dedicated dose protocol here yet; regimen shown as guidance.
bullets: Dabrafenib + trametinib, or encorafenib + binimetinib, for BRAF V600E disease
Chemo-immunotherapy is an alternative if targeted therapy is not tolerated
No StewardMD dose protocol for these combinations at present - prescribe per current label

nodes.name: KRAS G12C
nodes.title: KRAS G12C metastatic NSCLC: therapy
nodes.description: First line is usually chemo-immunotherapy; a KRAS G12C inhibitor is used after prior therapy. No dedicated dose protocol here yet.
bullets: First line: standard PD-L1 / chemo-immunotherapy (KRAS is not yet a first-line target)
After progression: sotorasib or adagrasib (KRAS G12C inhibitors)
No StewardMD dose protocol for KRAS G12C inhibitors at present - prescribe per current label

nodes.name: MET exon-14
nodes.title: MET exon-14 skipping metastatic NSCLC: targeted therapy
nodes.description: A MET inhibitor is preferred. No dedicated dose protocol here yet; regimen shown as guidance.
bullets: Capmatinib or tepotinib for MET exon-14 skipping alterations
Chemo-immunotherapy is an alternative first line if a MET inhibitor is unavailable
No StewardMD dose protocol for MET inhibitors at present - prescribe per current label

nodes.name: RET fusion
nodes.title: RET-rearranged metastatic NSCLC: targeted therapy
nodes.description: A selective RET inhibitor is preferred. No dedicated dose protocol here yet; regimen shown as guidance.
bullets: Selpercatinib or pralsetinib for RET fusion-positive disease
Chemo-immunotherapy is an alternative if a RET inhibitor is not tolerated
No StewardMD dose protocol for RET inhibitors at present - prescribe per current label

nodes.name: PD-L1 expression
nodes.title: Driver-negative metastatic NSCLC: PD-L1 tumor proportion score
nodes.description: For driver-negative disease, PD-L1 expression guides single-agent immunotherapy vs chemo-immunotherapy.

nodes.name: PD-L1-high IO
nodes.title: Driver-negative, PD-L1 >= 50%: immunotherapy
nodes.description: Single-agent pembrolizumab is a preferred option; chemo-immunotherapy is an alternative, matched to histology.
bullets: Single-agent pembrolizumab (preferred for high PD-L1, good performance status)
Platinum chemo-immunotherapy is a reasonable alternative, especially for bulky/symptomatic disease
Match the chemotherapy backbone to histology (pemetrexed non-squamous only)
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Chemo-immunotherapy
nodes.title: Driver-negative, PD-L1 < 50%: chemo-immunotherapy
nodes.description: Platinum chemo-immunotherapy, matched to histology (pembrolizumab + pemetrexed-platinum for non-squamous; pembrolizumab + carboplatin-taxane for squamous).
bullets: Non-squamous: pembrolizumab + platinum + pemetrexed
Squamous: pembrolizumab + carboplatin + a taxane
Chemotherapy alone if immunotherapy is contraindicated
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: NSCLC surveillance
nodes.title: NSCLC: surveillance after curative-intent therapy
nodes.description: Follow-up after curative resection or chemoradiation; investigate new symptoms promptly.
bullets: History, physical and contrast CT chest every 6 months for 2-3 years, then annually (annual low-dose CT long-term)
Smoking cessation support at every visit
No routine brain MRI or PET in asymptomatic patients; image on symptoms
Biopsy suspected recurrence and re-profile molecular markers
nodes.linkLabel: If recurrence / metastatic disease: enter the driver-directed metastatic pathway

nodes.name: SCLC workup
nodes.title: SCLC: workup and staging
nodes.description: Small cell lung cancer is aggressive and usually disseminated; complete staging including brain imaging drives the limited vs extensive decision.
bullets: History, physical, performance status; paraneoplastic review (SIADH, Cushing, LEMS)
Contrast CT chest/abdomen/pelvis and PET-CT
Brain MRI (or CT) for all patients - CNS involvement is common
Bloods including LDH, sodium and marrow-reserve assessment before chemotherapy

nodes.name: SCLC stage
nodes.title: SCLC: stage
nodes.description: Limited-stage disease fits a tolerable radiation field and is treated with concurrent chemoradiation; extensive-stage adds immunotherapy to chemotherapy; relapse follows a distinct track.

tables.title: SCLC stage and default approach
rows: Confined to one hemithorax / a safe RT field (roughly I-III)
Beyond a tolerable RT field / distant metastases (IV)

nodes.name: Limited-stage SCLC
nodes.title: Limited-stage SCLC: chemoradiation
nodes.description: Platinum-etoposide with concurrent thoracic radiation; consider prophylactic cranial irradiation in responders.
bullets: Cisplatin (or carboplatin) + etoposide for 4 cycles
Concurrent thoracic radiotherapy started early (twice-daily or high-dose once-daily)
Prophylactic cranial irradiation for responders after chemoradiation
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Extensive-stage SCLC
nodes.title: Extensive-stage SCLC: chemo-immunotherapy
nodes.description: Platinum-etoposide with an added checkpoint inhibitor (atezolizumab or durvalumab), continued as maintenance.
bullets: Carboplatin + etoposide + atezolizumab, or platinum-etoposide + durvalumab, then immunotherapy maintenance
Consider consolidative thoracic radiation in selected responders and PCI or MRI surveillance for the brain
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Relapsed SCLC
nodes.title: Relapsed SCLC: second-line therapy
nodes.description: Second-line therapy guided by the interval since first-line platinum.
bullets: Platinum-sensitive relapse (>= ~6 months): re-challenge with platinum-etoposide
Platinum-resistant relapse: topotecan, lurbinectedin, or a taxane / other single agent
Best supportive care for poor performance status
Regimen referenced below

nodes.name: SCLC surveillance
nodes.title: SCLC: surveillance after therapy
nodes.description: Frequent follow-up given the high relapse rate; act quickly on progression.
bullets: History, physical and CT imaging every 2-3 months in year 1, lengthening thereafter
Brain MRI surveillance if PCI was omitted
Smoking cessation support at every visit
nodes.linkLabel: On relapse: enter the second-line SCLC pathway

nodes.name: Mesothelioma workup
nodes.title: Mesothelioma: workup and histology
nodes.description: Confirm mesothelioma and its histologic subtype; subtype and resectability drive therapy.
bullets: Asbestos-exposure history; contrast CT chest/abdomen and PET-CT
Adequate tissue (thoracoscopic biopsy preferred) for subtype: epithelioid vs sarcomatoid/biphasic
Pleural fluid cytology alone is insufficient for definitive subtyping
Pulmonary and cardiac function assessment if aggressive surgery is contemplated

nodes.name: Mesothelioma resectability
nodes.title: Mesothelioma: resectable vs advanced
nodes.description: A minority of early epithelioid tumors are candidates for multimodality surgery; most patients present with unresectable disease treated systemically.

nodes.name: Resectable mesothelioma
nodes.title: Resectable mesothelioma: multimodality therapy
nodes.description: Selected early epithelioid disease treated with surgery combined with chemotherapy and/or radiation at an experienced center.
bullets: Macroscopic complete resection (pleurectomy/decortication or extrapleural pneumonectomy) in fit, epithelioid, node-negative patients
Combine with cisplatin-pemetrexed chemotherapy (neoadjuvant or adjuvant) +/- radiation
Manage only at high-volume centers; benefit of aggressive surgery remains debated
Chemotherapy regimen referenced below

nodes.name: Mesothelioma histology
nodes.title: Advanced mesothelioma: histologic subtype
nodes.description: Subtype guides the first-line choice between chemotherapy and dual immunotherapy; non-epithelioid tumors derive greater relative benefit from immunotherapy.

nodes.name: Advanced epithelioid mesothelioma
nodes.title: Advanced epithelioid mesothelioma: systemic therapy
nodes.description: Either platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy or nivolumab-ipilimumab immunotherapy is acceptable first line for epithelioid disease.
bullets: Cisplatin (or carboplatin) + pemetrexed, with the option to add a VEGF inhibitor
Nivolumab + ipilimumab is an alternative first-line option
Regimens referenced below

nodes.name: Advanced non-epithelioid mesothelioma
nodes.title: Advanced non-epithelioid mesothelioma: dual immunotherapy
nodes.description: Nivolumab-ipilimumab is preferred for sarcomatoid / biphasic disease, which responds poorly to chemotherapy.
bullets: Nivolumab + ipilimumab is the preferred first-line therapy
Platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy if immunotherapy is contraindicated
Regimens referenced below
